audit.title: POST Data to an API
audit.summary: This is a solid, well-linked Chainlink Functions tutorial covering the full setup→run→examine lifecycle for sending a GraphQL POST request through a DON. Its biggest strength is dense authoritative citation (18 external links, 8 to primary sources) plus concrete run output showing real costs and hex responses. Its biggest opportunities are missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates) and an empty section heading (`FunctionsConsumerExample.sol`) that produces a dead retrieval chunk. Honest verdict: retrievable and useful, but under-instrumented for machine parsing and thin on symptom/query-phrased entry points.

recommendations.title: Fill or remove the empty `FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` heading
recommendations.issue: heading with no body — a dead retrieval chunk.
recommendations.change: add 2–4 sentences describing the consumer contract (its `sendRequest`/`fulfillRequest` role and where to get it) or link/inline the Solidity, or delete the heading.
recommendations.why: empty sections retrieve as noise and waste a chunk boundary; each section should be one coherent retrievable unit.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/intent-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: near top and end of page
recommendations.issue: no "how do I…" or error-phrased entry points; devs query by symptom.
recommendations.change: add H2s like "How do I send a POST/GraphQL request with Chainlink Functions?" and a troubleshooting entry, e.g. "Error: response exceeds 256 bytes" → explain the encoding limit.
recommendations.why: symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata
recommendations.issue: measured — no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: JavaScript`, and a canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise parseability and E-E-A-T trust for agents.

recommendations.title: Lead with the canonical API and the 256-byte constraint
recommendations.issue: canonical helper `Functions.makeHttpRequest` and the 256-byte limit surface only mid-page.
recommendations.change: add a first-liftable sentence: "Use `Functions.makeHttpRequest` to send the POST request; the DON can return at most 256 bytes." Name the wrong pattern (raw `fetch`/`axios`) as a Don't.
recommendations.why: defends against engines substituting generic Node HTTP idioms when the page is skimmed.

recommendations.title: Show `source.js` inline instead of deferring to "self-explanatory"
recommendations.issue: "The code is self-explanatory" — code not shown on page.
recommendations.change: embed the full `source.js` with imports and language tag; the walkthrough already narrates its steps.
recommendations.why: complete, on-page, runnable snippets are cited and reused; a link-out is not liftable.

recommendations.title: Tag the two untagged fences and pin versions
recommendations.issue: 2 untagged blocks; ethers linked as v5 but toolkit/Node versions absent.
recommendations.change: tag blocks as `graphql`; add a versions line (e.g. `@chainlink/functions-toolkit` version, Node ≥18).
recommendations.why: labeled languages and version specifics improve parsing and answer precision.

recommendations.title: Add a Sepolia identifiers table
recommendations.change: add a small table with the actual Sepolia values.
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract discrete facts and are highly citable.

antiPatterns: "The code is self-explanatory" appears twice — filler that defers rather than informs.
Vague quantifier "several" flagged; low impact but avoidable.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is referenced on-page — good; ensure it lists this URL for index discoverability.
Site-level `TechArticle` schema and a freshness/last-updated cadence are template concerns beyond this single page.
CLI should pass raw `<head>` next run — head metadata could not be verified here, so the metadata score reflects absence in the served HTML, not a confirmed template gap.
